thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV:high — inference-p95-latency for prod-redwood-east above 1400ms for 3 consecutive mins. Recent deploy? Links: https://perf.redwood/inference/alerts/1785432109

maya (oncall): seeing it, pulling traces now. pinging noah for runtime kernel weirdness.

noah (runtime): on it — I see increased tail latency on 4 GPUs in pool-dedicated-2. KV cache miss rate jumped ~18% around the same time. Not seeing errors, just much higher p95.

maya (oncall): rolling blacklist on incoming batched requests from one high qps client to rule out bad traffic: `kubectl patch svc batch-ingress -p '{"spec":{"externalTrafficPolicy":"Local"}}'` (will revert).

alex (support): FYI we have one customer reporting slowness (ticket #INC-1348) — they say responses are hanging for 10-20s.

noah (runtime): can reproduce via replaying sample request load — looks like a specific request shape triggers long KV lookups. Dumping logs to /tmp/kv-slow.log and sending to slack thread.

maya (oncall): paging PD now for escalation if we can't stabilize in 10 min. @ria can you standby for infra stuff?

ria (sre): here. I can scale pool-dedicated-2 by +2 GPUs as quick mitigation if needed. Would that mask root cause?

noah (runtime): it might reduce queueing but won't fix KV miss pattern. Suggest quick patch: enable short-lived local prefix cache for that model to avoid remote KV hits. Patch tested in staging, looks safe.

maya (oncall): go for it, noah. Apply patch and monitor.

noah (runtime): patch applied at 1785432128 — enabling local-prefix-cache=true for model redwood-rt-1. Watching metrics.

alerting-bot: :information_source: Deploy recorded: runtime/noah enabled local-prefix-cache redwood-rt-1 @ 1785432128 (sha abc123).

noah (runtime): p95 dropped to ~420ms after ~40s, KV miss down to 3%. Confirming mitigation holds.

maya (oncall): nice. scaling back the temporary pod increase, leave the cache patch. Reverting the earlier `kubectl patch` on ingress.

ria (sre): scaling back +2 GPUs now. All green.

alex (support): updated customer INC-1348 — told them we applied mitigation, asked for confirmation if they still see slowness.

sam (product): quick question — what's the SLO exposure here and do we need an incident page to exec? We should decide whether this is a paged incident vs ticket for future recurrences.

maya (oncall): SLO dip was ~0.4% over 15m window — not a big customer-wide outage but customer-visible tail impact. I think it's borderline. We need to reduce noise while still catching tail regressions.

ria (sre): post-incident action items: (1) add dashboard tile for KV miss rate by model and pool, (2) tune alert thresholds so we page only when p95 > 1500ms AND KV_miss_rate > 10% for 3m, (3) create runbook for enabling local-prefix-cache.

noah (runtime): +1 on runbook. Also propose a short-term alert rule change: current alert pages on p95 > 1200ms alone — change to page only if p95 > 1500ms OR (p95>1200ms AND KV_miss_rate>12%). Everything else should create a ticket in #eng-sre for follow-up.

maya (oncall): agreed. We should also map sev assignment: if a single customer reports hanging responses with matching tail spike, route page to eng-oncall + support; if system-wide p95 spike without customer reports, route to eng-sre but as ticket unless p95>2000ms.

sam (product): sounds reasonable. We need to avoid chasing noisy p95 blips due to heavy one-off clients. Product would like a notification to owners of models with frequent KV misses.

alerting-bot: proposed rule diff:```
- alert: inference_p95_latency
  expr: p95_inference_ms > 1200
  severity: page
  channels: [eng-oncall]
+ alert: inference_p95_latency
  expr: p95_inference_ms > 1500
  severity: page
  channels: [eng-oncall]
+ alert: inference_p95_latency_kv_combo
  expr: p95_inference_ms > 1200 and kv_miss_rate > 0.12
  severity: page
  channels: [eng-oncall, eng-sre]
```

maya (oncall): I'll create the ticket to update the Prometheus rules and add the dashboard request. Assigning to ria for infra changes and to noah for the runtime runbook.

ria (sre): filing infra ticket now — TKT-2987 — includes hours for dashboard dev and alert rule change.

noah (runtime): I'll write the runbook and add a short snippet for safe toggle: ```sh
# enable local prefix cache
curl -X POST $CONTROLPLANE/api/models/redwood-rt-1/config -d '{"local_prefix_cache":true}'
```

maya (oncall): postmortem note: root cause likely a regression in remote KV latency combined with a high-QPS client pattern. Mitigation was to enable local cache and scale temporarily. Permanent fixes: runbook + alert tuning + dashboard + follow-up with platform team to investigate KV backend.

alex (support): customer ACKed improvement. Closing INC-1348 after 30m if no further reports.

sam (product): please add a scheduled review with product + runtime to evaluate whether model-level autoscaling or per-client rate-limiting is needed.

maya (oncall): adding that as an action item to the ticket. Summary: incident mitigated, follow-ups decided: update alert thresholds, add dashboard, create runtime runbook, follow-up KV root-cause investigation, clarify page vs ticket mapping. I'll hand this off to ria for infra work and noah for runtime docs. Thanks everyone. :tada:
